question: Which term is used to denote the mean income computed for every man, woman, and child in a particular group including those living in group quarters?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Per capita income**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Per capita income** is the term used to denote the mean income computed for every man, woman, and child in a particular group, including those living in group quarters.
 
• It is a measure of the **average income earned per person** in a given area in a specified year.
 
• This metric is used to compare the economic well-being of different populations or to track the economic progress of a region over time.
 
• Per capita income helps in understanding the **standard of living **and economic health of a population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Per capita income** is calculated by dividing the total income of a particular area by its population.
 
• It is often used in economic studies and reports to provide a more accurate representation of individual prosperity than total income or GDP alone.
 
• While it is a useful measure, it does not account for income distribution within the population.
 
• Higher per capita income generally indicates a higher standard of living and better economic conditions.
